text:
jamal: heads-up — after yesterday's allocator tuning (workspace bump + eager-free), we're seeing ~3x more OOMs on p3-prod for long-context generation (>2k tokens). Repro is easy with the stress script. nvml logs show fragmentation spikes around the time of OOM.

sri: ugh. which commit? thread ts/PR?

jamal: commit c7f9b2e (allocator: increase initial workspace to 512MB, enable eager_free). rolled to prod 02:10UTC. failing on routes with prefix cache hits + long continuations. quick paste from the profiler: 

```
# profiler snapshot (trimmed)
active_alloc_bytes=6.1GB
total_reserved_bytes=8.3GB
largest_free_chunk=32MB
num_free_chunks=412
kv_cache_mem=1.8GB
workspace_resident=560MB
fragmentation_ratio=1.36
peak_alloc=7.9GB
OOM at step: generate_token(1873)
```

jamal: also saw lots of small free chunks instead of a handful of big ones -> fragmentation.

marta: do we have GC/eager-free stats? eager-free might be racing with reuse leading to allocator churn. Any per-kernel workspace sizing changes?

jamal: kernel selector left unchanged, but batching heuristics got a tweak to default to larger batch windows (to improve throughput) which increases simultaneous workspace concurrency. Combined with larger initial workspace seems to push fragmentation/OOM.

sri: plausible. two levers to try: 1) reduce initial workspace size (e.g. 256MB), 2) enable buffer-reuse path (reuse small buffers rather than free/alloc). The latter was behind a flag.

marta: Agree. Also for prefix cache: we should consider memory budgeting — the prefix cache TTL and shard sizing are amplifying memory pressure. Right now prefix_cache.ttl=24h and shard_count=4 which keeps large contiguous allocations. If we increase shard_count and reduce TTL, we can bound per-shard resident memory. Tradeoff: hit-rate will drop somewhat. We measured this in staging: TTL 24h -> 1h reduced hit-rate ~7% but freed ~40% of memory in busy shards.

jamal: here's the quick config I want to test in canary: 

```
serving:
  allocator:
    workspace_mb: 256
    reuse_buffers: true
  prefix_cache:
    ttl_hours: 1
    shard_count: 16
    per_shard_max_mb: 512
  batching:
    max_window_ms: 30   # reduce from 80
```

jamal: repro command for the stress runner: 

```
./tools/stress_runner --model redwood-small --ctx 4096 --parallel 12 --prefix-cache-on
# watch logs: tail -f /var/log/redwood/serve.log | grep OOM
```

taylo: deploy-bot: canary scheduled for 6 nodes in us-west-2. I'll roll the allocator/ttl changes to canary first. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for commit c7f9b2e-alloc-fix to cluster p3-prod-canary (6 nodes)

marta: we should also add a quick telemetry point: emit per-shard resident bytes and prefix_cache.hit_rate every 1min to detect regression early. Also add a synthetic workload to measure hit-rate delta.

sri: Agree. One more note: kernel selection fallback when the sequence length > 2k currently picks the big-kernel optimized for throughput, which has larger temp buffers. For these long sequences, we might prefer the memory-optimized kernel even if latency slightly increases. Let's add a policy: if free_mem_ratio < 0.15 then prefer mem-optimized kernels for >1k tokens.

jamal: good idea. Quick stat from staging with mem-optimized kernel: temp buffer drop from ~700MB -> ~320MB per invocation, latency +8ms P99 but no OOMs.

marta: action items:
- taylo to roll canary with config above (allocator workspace=256, reuse=true, prefix TTL=1h, shards=16) — ETA 10m (taylo)
- deploy-bot to monitor prefix_cache.hit_rate and per_shard_resident metrics and alert if hit_rate drops >15%
- jamal to run stress_runner against canary and post profiler snapshots
- sri to add kernel-selection memory-threshold policy PR (small patch)

jamal: running stress now against canary (started 02:48UTC). Will paste profiler after 2mins.

[~70s later]

jamal: quick post-canary profile: 
```
active_alloc_bytes=4.2GB
total_reserved_bytes=5.1GB
largest_free_chunk=1.2GB
num_free_chunks=18
kv_cache_mem=980MB
workspace_resident=260MB
fragmentation_ratio=1.12
peak_alloc=4.9GB
no OOMs after 5k tokens across runs
prefix_cache.hit_rate=0.83 (was 0.9 in prod)
```

marta: looks promising. hit_rate drop to 0.83 from 0.9 matches earlier sim. that should be acceptable vs 3x OOMs.

sri: let's keep canary for 1h and if stable promote, and open a follow-up to tune shard sizing per-tenant. Also note we should add an automated mem-pressure fallback to reduce batch window dynamically (batching.max_window_ms) to keep concurrency lower under memory pressure.

taylo: canary held stable for 45m, no OOM alerts, promoting now. Will keep monitoring.

jamal: thanks all — will write up a short postmortem with config numbers and a perf note: memory-optimized kernel tradeoffs, reuse_buffer gains, and prefix-cache TTL vs hit_rate curve.

marta: add the perf graphs to the console dashboard and put an alert for fragmentation_ratio > 1.25.

sri: nice work team.
